API: materialize_synthetic_capsule(destination: Path, members: tuple[NamespaceMember,...], *, protected_roots: CapsuleProtectedRoots) -> SourceTree
CapsuleProtectedRoots: frozen dataclass with exactly raw, auth, profile, controller, public; every field is an existing root-supplied DirectoryIdentity. Missing policy is not allowed. These are protected locations, not files to read.
SCAP01: Validate all five directory identities via canonical path + O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW held descriptor, device/inode/type/current-owner before any destination write. Destination must be neither equal to nor ancestor/descendant of any protected root. Protected roots may overlap one another; requiring independent role locations would be an unnecessary restriction. Recheck identities/disjointness before return. Do not read their contents or create them in real provisioning.
SCAP02: Retain original bounded source bytes, derive expected source_closure/v1 digest from exact25 source paths and four empty init files at mode0600/four fixed directories at0700. Derivation is independent of destination bytes. After all writes, hold destination root identity and reopen each expected file relative to it, checking byte equality/mode/owner/singlelink/stable fd/named identity. Reopen original source bindings. Compare final capture_tree full digest to expected recipe, not counts alone; recheck held root and final bytes after capture before return.
tests: Before patch reproduce actual accepted protected-profile path and late same-size destination mutation. After patch, explicit-policy missing/invalid/directory replacement/equality/ancestor/descendant tests; source/empty-init/late-mutation/normal digest positives and no protected content reads. Synthetic filesystem only; copied code never imported.
nonclaims: Root selects the real protected identities and independently approved member hashes. This enforces the supplied exact identities; it cannot discover omitted true roots. No atomic execution/hostile same-UID mutator/OS secrecy claim. Partial destinations remain and cannot be retried.
